I think it is the primary concept of post-positivism - we can use evidence in the world to disprove ideas about the world, but we cannot prove anything so conclusively that it can't be potentially be falsified by future data.

Post-positivism is the philosophy that basically ended up underpinning modern science, which keeps modern research adaptable and skeptical, essentially preventing any one theory from becoming a religious truth. Of course, not every scientist expresses this philosophy consistently about their pet theories, but the fact that it's so widely accepted encourages researchers to replace bad ideas even if they were long thought true. Who knows where our technology and world views would be without this.
